1 مَجَدَ , aor.
مَجُدَ , inf. n. مَجْدٌ; (L, K;) and مَجُدَ, aor.
مَجُدَ , inf. n. مَجَادَةٌ; (S, L, K;) He (a man, S) was, or became, possessed of, or characterized by, مَجْد [or glory, honour, dignity, nobility, &c.; he was, or became, glorious, in a state of honour or dignity, noble, &c.: see مَجْدٌ below]. (S, L, K.) ―
-b2- See 3. ―
-b3- مَجَدَتِ الإِبِلُ, (AZ, IAar, S, L, K,) aor.
مَجُدَ , (AZ, L,) inf. n. مَجْدٌ (AZ, L, K) and مُجُودٌ; (AZ, S, L, K;) and ↓ امجدت ; (L, K;) The camels fed in a land abounding with pasturage, and satiated themselves therewith: (AZ, L:) or, lighted upon abundant pasturage: (IAar, L, K:) or, obtained of fresh herbage, (خَلًى, S, K,) or of herbage, (L,) nearly as much as satiated them, (S, L, K,) and their bodies made this known. (L.) See 4. ―
-b4- مَجَدَتِ الغَنَمُ, inf. n. مُجُودٌ, The sheep, or goats, ate of leguminous plants so as to blunt the sharpness of their hunger. (A.) ―
-b5- [Hence, app., accord. to the A, the signification of مَجَدَ and مَجُدَ given in the commencement of this art.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
